subject: Request: VM evidence and attestation after vendor-delayed CVE remediation
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlasfin.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: security@atlasfin.com
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: CVE follow-up and request for remediation evidence (CVE-2027-4581)

Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick response earlier on the call. As discussed, our internal tooling flagged an exposure linked to CVE-2027-4581 in the third-party image-handling library used by one of your services. Atlas requires:

- Scan evidence demonstrating the vulnerable package was detected in our customer-facing environment (we've already seen the scanner finding).
- A remediation timeline and confirmation of patch deployment or compensating controls for any service where the vendor patch was delayed.
- A short attestation we can archive for our audit (SOC2) saying Redwood either patched or implemented a compensating control and the window to closure.

We understand there was a vendor delay and are open to an exception if you provide clear evidence and a firm closure date. Can you send the scan exports, patch proof, and an attestation doc by next week? If a formal SLA exception is required, please indicate the duration and mitigation.

Thanks,
Laura Chen\Security Engineering\Atlas Financial

Attachment: atlas-scan-finding-20280209.json (we saw this in our portal)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlasfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CVE follow-up and request for remediation evidence (CVE-2027-4581)

Laura — thank you for the clear ask and for flagging the finding. We're treating this as high priority. Summary and immediate plan below: 

1) Scope: Impact observed in the media-processing tier for requests routed through gateway region-us-east-1. No customer data exfiltration observed; this is a remote code execution vector in a third-party image library (CVE-2027-4581).

2) What happened: vendor released a fix 2028-02-07 but delayed signed binaries until 2028-02-09 due to internal CI issues. We validated the vendor patch and have started staged rollout.

3) Immediate mitigations in place (today):
   - WAF rule deployed to block suspicious image payloads (latency <5ms addition).
   - Rate limiting tightened to 5r/s per client for image endpoints.
   - Temporary kill-switch on batch image transforms for customers flagged by your scanner (Atlas flagged ids).

4) Evidence we will provide by Tue 2028-02-14:
   - Full scan export from our environment (CSV) showing initial detection timestamp and affected hosts.
   - Patch deployment manifest and service restart logs.
   - Signed attestation PDF outlining exception rationale and closure ETA (we'll include an SLA exception length).

Ben, Monica — can you assemble the scan export and patch proofs into a single evidence packet and draft the attestation? Jonas, can you confirm rollback/rollback-proof isn't required and that the staged rollout covers all customer-facing pools?

Laura — we will upload the packet to a shared drive link and email you when it's ready. If you need a DocuSign-backed attestation, say the word and we'll route it.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart\Head of Trust & Safety\Redwood Inference

----
Forwarded attachment note: "We saw the Atlas portal export attached. We'll correlate."

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlasfin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2028 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CVE follow-up and request for remediation evidence (CVE-2027-4581)

Laura / team — attaching the evidence exports as discussed. Summary of attached items: 

- atlas-202801-scan-summary.csv: scan timestamp (2028-02-09T02:13:45Z) + hostlist + package version (libimg 4.1.2 vulnerable; patched to 4.1.3).
- cve-2027-4581-patchproof.tar.gz: deployment manifest (services/media-pool-1..4), systemd restart logs showing restart shards completed, and hashes of the deployed binary matching vendor-signed checksums.
- sla-exception-request.pdf: drafted exception request (length: 7 days) explaining vendor-signed binary delay and compensating controls (WAF, rate limit).

Attestation text (drafted below) — please review and confirm if OK to sign: 

"Redwood Inference attests that service 'media-transform' in region us-east-1 detected a vulnerable third-party component (CVE-2027-4581) on 2028-02-09. Due to a vendor-supplied binary signing delay, a staged patch rollout was completed starting 2028-02-11 and verified fully deployed to customer-facing pools on 2028-02-13. Compensating controls (WAF rule and client-rate limiting) were applied 2028-02-10. Redwood requests a 7-day SLA exception window covering 2028-02-09 through 2028-02-16 to account for staged rollout and verification. Evidence packet (scan exports and deployment proofs) is attached and available via shared drive link.

Signed — Ben Carter, Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference"

Evelyn / Monica — please confirm the dates in the attestation match operational logs. Laura — let me know if you prefer a DocuSign-signed PDF; we can route it today.

Attachments: atlas-202801-scan-summary.csv, cve-2027-4581-patchproof.tar.gz, sla-exception-request.pdf
